data.why: jdaviz's own imviz test fixtures are small synthetic FITS images (a base exposure, a block-reduced copy, and a block-reduced+rotated copy of the same field) plus a DS9 region file, which together exercise linking/blinking, orientation and aperture photometry without needing a MAST login or download.

goals: Load a JWST/HST-like FITS image and inspect it: pan, zoom, change stretch and colormap
Load a second, offset/rotated exposure of the same field, link the two by WCS, and blink-compare them
Import a DS9 region (ds9_annulus_01.reg) or draw a circular/annular aperture and run Aperture Photometry on a source
Mark a spatial subset and inspect or export its metadata and statistics
Switch to a spectral or cube configuration (Specviz/Cubeviz) and fit a line or extract a 1D spectrum on a loaded cube/spectrum

review.summary: The imaging part of the tree is accurate and well staged: loading, aligning on the sky, blinking, restyling and aperture photometry all match the screens, and the photometry feature is a good lift-able unit. But it covers only the image side of a tool the README describes as spanning images, spectra and cubes, and some of its actions record the agent's struggle rather than the workflow, so it needs scoping and cleanup before filing.
